title: Valid Parenthesis String
pattern: Greedy: track the range of possible open brackets
statement: A string contains `(`, `)` and `*`. Each `*` may be treated as `(`, as `)` or as an empty string. Return `True` if the string can be made into a valid parenthesis string.

example.why: Treat the * as an opening bracket: (()) is valid.

idea: Without stars, one counter of currently open brackets is enough. A star makes that count **uncertain** — so track the whole **range** of possible counts: `lower` (fewest open brackets possible) and `upper` (most possible).

`(` raises both ends, `)` lowers both. A `*` lowers `lower` (if used as `)`) and raises `upper` (if used as `(`). `lower` is kept at 0 or above, because scenarios with a negative count are simply invalid.
If `upper` drops below 0, even the most generous reading has too many `)` → `False`. At the end the string is valid exactly when 0 is in the range, i.e. `lower == 0`.

complexity.timeWhy: One pass over the string, with O(1) work per character.

steps.text: Our example: **`s = "(*))"`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`lower` … `upper` is the range of how many brackets could be open right now, over all ways of reading the stars. Before any character: exactly 0.
`(` opens a bracket in every reading: the range becomes **1 … 1**.
`*` could close a bracket (lower − 1), open one (upper + 1), or do nothing: the range widens to **0 … 2**.
`)` closes a bracket in every reading: the range becomes **0 … 1**. (`lower` is never allowed below 0 — readings that close more than is open are simply discarded.)
`)` closes a bracket in every reading: the range becomes **0 … 0**. (`lower` is never allowed below 0 — readings that close more than is open are simply discarded.)
The string is used up and the range is 0 … 0. It includes 0, so some reading leaves **no bracket open** → **True**.
Done — the answer is **`True`**. Treat the * as an opening bracket: (()) is valid.
